assistant|clustering_recommendation: Recommends starting with k-means clustering as it is straightforward and efficient
assistant|kmeans_strengths: K-means is good for distinct well-separated clusters, speed and efficiency, and easy interpretation
assistant|kmeans_limitations: K-means is sensitive to initial centroid placement, assumes spherical clusters, and requires predefined number of clusters
assistant|hierarchical_clustering_streng: Hierarchical clustering identifies nested structures, needs no predefined cluster number, and handles varying densities and shapes
assistant|hierarchical_clustering_limita: Hierarchical clustering is computationally expensive, dendrogram difficult to interpret, and sensitive to distance metrics
assistant|cluster_count_method_elbow: Elbow Method: plot WCSS against k; the flattening elbow point indicates optimal cluster count
assistant|cluster_count_method_silhouett: Silhouette Analysis: higher average silhouette score indicates well-separated and cohesive clusters
assistant|cluster_count_method_gap_stati: Gap Statistic: compares log(WCSS) with expected value under null reference; optimal k maximizes the gap
assistant|cluster_count_method_calinski_: Calinski-Harabasz Index: ratio of between-cluster to within-cluster variance; optimal k maximizes this index
assistant|cluster_count_method_davies_bo: Davies-Bouldin Index: measures cluster similarity via centroid distances and scatter; optimal k minimizes this index
assistant|cluster_count_method_visual_in: Visual Inspection: plot data using PCA or t-SNE and visually inspect clusters
assistant|cluster_count_method_cross_val: Cross-Validation: split data, apply k-means with different k values, evaluate performance on testing set
assistant|cluster_count_method_informati: Information Criteria (AIC/BIC): optimal number of clusters minimizes AIC or BIC value
assistant|cluster_count_recommendation: Recommends starting with elbow method and silhouette analysis as they are easy to implement
assistant|data_prep_missing_values: Handle missing values by imputing with mean/median, using a specific value, or removing them
assistant|data_prep_scaling_standardizat: Standardization (Z-scoring): subtract mean and divide by standard deviation for each feature
assistant|data_prep_scaling_minmax: Min-Max Scaling: rescale features to a common range, usually between 0 and 1
assistant|data_prep_log_transformation: Log Transformation: apply logarithmic transformation to skewed features to reduce outlier effects
assistant|data_prep_feature_selection: Select relevant features; remove features with low variance or high correlation with other features
assistant|data_prep_categorical_encoding: Transform categorical features into numerical features using one-hot encoding or label encoding
assistant|data_prep_outliers: Handle outliers by removing, transforming them, or using robust clustering algorithms
assistant|scaling_recommendation: For customer data, normalize or scale features like age, income, and purchase history to the same scale
assistant|visualization_scatter_plots: Scatter plots visualize relationships between two features, identifying correlations, outliers, and potential clusters
assistant|visualization_pairwise_scatter: Pairwise scatter plots visualize relationships between multiple features to identify correlations and clusters
assistant|visualization_heatmaps: Heatmaps visualize the correlation matrix to identify highly correlated features and potential clusters
assistant|visualization_box_plots: Box plots visualize distribution of individual features, identifying outliers and comparing distributions
assistant|visualization_histograms: Histograms visualize distribution shape and frequency of individual features
assistant|visualization_dimensionality_r: Dimensionality reduction techniques PCA, t-SNE, or UMAP visualize high-dimensional data in 2D or 3D
assistant|visualization_interactive: Interactive visualizations like interactive scatter plots, heatmaps, or parallel coordinates allow detailed data exploration
assistant|visualization_tools: Recommended tools: Matplotlib and Seaborn in Python, ggplot2 and plotly in R, Tableau, Power BI, or D3.js
